IncidentBot: P1 ALERT — LatticeCore (private VPC) auth proxy errors: high 5xx and mTLS handshake failures observed from 1956669950. Paging oncall.
PagerDuty: Paging Maya L. (oncall): urgent -> see #incidents for details
Maya L.: On it. Brief summary? Which service is flapping?
IncidentBot: Affected: auth-proxy (tenant=latticecore) behind edge-lb. Symptoms: client TLS handshake failures (tls_alert_bad_certificate) and downstream 401/403 for OIDC flows. Error rate spike ~200 eps at 1956669960.
Priya S. (Customer Success): LatticeCore reports users intermittently unable to log in via SSO. They see client cert rejections and secondarily 401 when tokens are exchanged. They said they rotated certs at 02:00 local before our morning window.
Tomas R. (Platform): Checking per-tenant cert store and vault rotations. I see a recent cert write for tenant latticecore at 1956669400 with fingerprint 9a:bc:...; but the active cert attached to auth-proxy pods still shows older fingerprint 3f:de:... Possibly rollout inconsistency.
Carla S. (Eng Infra): That could explain TLS handshake failures (client presents new cert, server expects CA chain?). Also seeing OIDC JWKS verification errors in logs: 'kid not found' for tokens issued after 1956669405. Looks like simultaneous JWKS rotation and mTLS cert roll.
Maya L.: Can we confirm whether our auth-proxy pulls certs from the tenant secret or from the local disk mount?
Tomas R.: It's mounted from a sidecar syncer. Sidecar logs show repeated 500s when fetching secret from vault-proxy for tenant latticecore between 1956669480..1956669520.
DevOps-bot: vault-proxy: 502 Bad Gateway -> upstream auth (vault) returned 502 (connection reset).
Maya L.: So sequence might be: customer rotates certs and JWKS almost simultaneously, our sidecar fails to fetch new secret/JWKS, auth-proxy still using old cert and old JWKS -> mTLS handshake fails for new clients and JWTs have unknown kid.
Priya S.: LatticeCore Ops: "We did a coordinated rotate for certs and OIDC key set at 02:01; we saw transient failures and rolled a partial rollback at 02:05 but users are still affected."
Carla S.: Short-term mitigation options: 1) Force auth-proxy to fall back to previous cert until sidecar sync recovers, 2) Increase JWKS accept window (not ideal), 3) Bypass sidecar and mount cert directly (risky). Recommend forcing a targeted restart of the sidecar and auth-proxy to pick current secret after clearing cache.
Maya L.: Agreed. I'll do a canary restart of sidecar+auth-proxy pair for one pod and monitor. Will also open a high-priority vault ticket.
[command]
kubectl -n latticecore rollout restart deployment/auth-proxy --selector=pod=canary-0
kubectl -n latticecore logs sidecar-syncer-canary-0 --since=10m | grep vault
[/command]

Maya L.: Canary restart applied. Logs show sidecar fetch succeeded on canary at 1956670045 and auth-proxy loaded new cert fingerprint 9a:bc:...; initial traffic shows significant reduction in tls_alert_bad_certificate for canary.
Tomas R.: Performing staggered restart across remaining pods with 30s delay. Also clearing JWKS cache per-tenant to force refetch: POST /admin/clear_jwks_cache?tenant=latticecore
[command]
curl -XPOST http://auth-proxy-admin.latticecore.svc/clear_jwks_cache?tenant=latticecore
kubectl -n latticecore exec sidecar-syncer-0 -- curl -sS http://vault-proxy.internal/secret/latticecore | jq .data
[/command]

DevOps-bot: JWKS cache cleared for tenant=latticecore, refetch status: 200 OK, keys fetched with kid=a1b2c3 (timestamp 1956670060).
LatticeCore Ops (customer): Confirmed: our OIDC rotated keys at 02:01 UTC, we see your sidecar pulled new keys at 02:10 UTC. We also reverted an automation that was pushing invalid cert chain. Rolling back that automation reduced errors by ~70%.
Maya L.: Monitoring metrics now: 5xxs and TLS alerts trending down to baseline by 1956670300. But we did accept some tokens that previously would have been rejected during the window because of temporary JWKS mismatch — need to quantify.
Alice M. (Security): Please collect a list of sessions accepted during 1956669900..1956670200 that had unknown kid accepted. We need to assess token auth acceptance risk and whether any expired/compromised keys were used.
Carla S.: Added structured debug logging for 'token_kid' and decision path for the affected window. Will export logs to secure bucket and share with Security.
Priya S.: LatticeCore: can you confirm whether any automated clients rotated both cert and keys via CI at once? This will help our post-incident guidance.
LatticeCore Ops (customer): We did run a combined job. It expected our internal vault to be available but the vault had a backing DB fail which caused the sidecar pulls to 502. We're opening a ticket with our infra team.
Maya L.: Impact summary (preliminary): ~40% of login attempts for LatticeCore tenant failed between 1956669950 and 1956670100, primarily for new client sessions and OIDC exchanges. No other tenants affected.
Maya L.: Action plan executed: canary restart (1956670045), full staggered restart (1956670105..1956670145), JWKS cache clear (1956670060). Monitoring shows errors falling to <1% above baseline by 1956670300.
Maya L.: Oncall handoff: Maya -> Tomas at 1956670600 (I have to step away at 23:40Z). Tomas will take pager for latticecore.
Tomas R.: Acknowledged. I'll be watching logs and the vault proxy queue.
Alice M.: Post-incident action items and owner assignment:
- (1) (Carla) Add guardrail that prevents simultaneous cert and JWKS automated rotations without coordination; require a 5min separation or an orchestration lock.
- (2) (Platform) Improve sidecar retry/backoff to avoid transient 502s causing sync failure; include exponential backoff and jitter.
- (3) (Security) Audit accepted tokens during window and report any suspicious activity (Alice).
- (4) (Customer Success + Eng) Create runbook for customers that do combined rotation procedures.
- (5) (SRE) Add an alert that triggers when per-tenant vault fetch error rate > 5% in 5m.
Priya S.: LatticeCore Ops: please provide timeline of your rotation and copy of CI job that performed rotation for the RCA. We'll coordinate a joint postmortem.
LatticeCore Ops (customer): Will share timeline and logs, appreciate the quick help.
Maya L.: I'm marking the incident as mitigated and closing the active page. Please file the postmortem and link it here.
IncidentBot: Incident mitigated — status set to 'mitigated' at 1956670320. Please attach postmortem artifacts.
Tomas R.: Leaving runbook notes: restarted sidecars + auth-proxy, cleared JWKS cache, validated cert fingerprints, increased sidecar fetch retries (temp). Reverted temporary changes at 1956671100.
Maya L.: Final note: consider adding a pre-flight job for customers to validate vault availability before doing mass rotation. It would've avoided this window.
Alice M.: Agree. Also, ensure the postmortem includes customer-approved next steps before closing the incident.
DevOps-bot: Attached logs: auth-proxy: TLS_ALERT_BAD_CERTIFICATE (1956669962..1956670128) and jwks: kid_not_found (1956669958..1956670099).
Priya S.: Customer said "thanks" — we prevented a more severe outage. We'll schedule a tabletop with LatticeCore next week.
Maya L.: Good work everyone.
